messages:
jordan-sales: Hey team — AcmeCorp POC: when they enable log export to our Console they see a burst of 429s and trace IDs aren't showing up in the Console dashboard. They want a fix + short note on expected per-GB pricing for logs. Can we swarm?

alex-eng: On it. Do we have a sample request/response with 429 headers? That will help triage Retry-After and rate-limit logic.

maria-sre: They mentioned using Fluent Bit to forward. Common issue: small bursts cause many concurrent connections, hitting the ingestion qps bucket.

jordan-sales: Yes they pasted this header from their side: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 60
X-Trace-Id: f2a9c1d0
```

sam-reliability: That Retry-After = 60s means our rate limiter kicked in. For POC we typically suggest client-side backoff + batching. We can also enable a temporary higher burst allowance on their org for the POC.

tara-se: Adding checklist: (1) confirm fluent-bit config, (2) ensure trace header preserved, (3) check Console ingestion metrics, (4) pricing note for logs.

ops-bot: Ingestion queue alert: org=acme-poc ingestion_rate=1400 qps_limit=1200 spike=200 timestamp=1778459100

alex-eng: Maria, can you share the minimal Fluent Bit output config we recommend to keep X-Trace-Id as a header?

maria-sre: Sure — sample snippet they should use (Fluent Bit output to HTTP):
```
[OUTPUT]
    Name  http
    Match *
    Host  logs.redwood.example
    Port  443
    URI   /v1/ingest
    Header X-API-Key ${API_KEY}
    Header X-Trace-Id $X_TRACE_ID
    tls   On
    Format json_lines
    tls.verify On
```
Note: Fluent Bit needs a filter to map trace id field into header if their client lib writes trace in body.

jordan-sales: They said trace is currently in payload as `trace_id` field.

alex-eng: Ok add this filter before output:
```
[FILTER]
    Name    modify
    Match   *
    Copy    trace_id X_TRACE_ID
```
That sets env var used in Header.

sam-reliability: Also recommend enabling batching (size/time) to reduce qps. Example: set Batch_Max_Size=1024 and Batch_Max_Timeout=5s on their side.

paul-security: Quick security note: AcmeCorp asked about retention + encryption for exported logs. For Private/Dedicated we support KMS; hosted logs are encrypted at rest and in transit. I'll DM the SOC2 attestation PDF.

jordan-sales: Great. Pricing: they want estimate for 2TB/month during POC then 10TB projected. Any quick numbers?

tara-se: Quick ballpark: POC tier = $0.10/GB ingest (discounted), production usage negotiable via committed capacity. I'll send formal quote.

alex-eng: Back to missing traces — if the trace header arrives at ingestion we index it and link to Console span view. If not visible, check ingestion parsing pipeline for `trace_id` field name mismatch. I can run a realtime query if they share one raw event.

acme-rep (shared by jordan-sales): here's a redacted sample event body they forwarded: 
```
{"timestamp":"2026-02-26T14:22:01Z","level":"info","msg":"response","trace_id":"f2a9c1d0","user":"u-123","latency_ms":42}
```

alex-eng: That should map. Two likely failure modes: (1) the header wasn't set so Console can't correlate; (2) ingestion parser failed due to charset or escaping.

maria-sre: I ran a quick tail on the ingestion pipeline — saw malformed JSON errors for some batches around 14:22:01. Likely Fluent Bit mixing mult-line logs. Recommend `multiline parser` off or proper parser config.

jordan-sales: Do we want to request they enable a temporary higher burst?

sam-reliability: Yes — for the POC we can uplift their org's burst to 2000 qps for 72h. I can apply if they confirm time window.

jordan-sales: I'll ask for a 72h window starting now.

deploy-bot: deploy request registered by sam-reliability for org acme-poc: increase.qps -> 2000, ttl=72h. ID=deploy-3342.

maria-sre: After uplift, we should still advise batching and backoff. Also set a header map so any 429 returns the X-Trace-Id back to client in body for easier triage.

alex-eng: For reproducibility, here's a curl pattern that includes trace header and shows how our ingestion echoes trace in the response body (in POC debug mode):
```
curl -X POST https://logs.redwood.example/v1/ingest \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-Trace-Id: test-abc-123' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"msg":"hi","trace_id":"test-abc-123"}'
# success -> 202 + {"trace_id":"test-abc-123"}
# rate limit -> 429 + {"trace_id":"test-abc-123","error":"rate_limited","retry_after":60}
```

jordan-sales: Perfect. I'll run that with the customer's sample to confirm echo.

paul-security: One more enterprise blocker: they asked about data residency for EU users. We have EU region support; need to confirm their org is scoped correctly. Tara, can you confirm region setting?

tara-se: They're currently on `us-west`. We can open a migration ticket to `eu-west-1` for production; for POC it's fine to stay US but flag for legal.

jordan-sales: Action items I have: (1) request 72h burst uplift — doing now, (2) send Fluent Bit snippet + batching/backoff docs, (3) confirm pricing email from Tara, (4) pass SOC2 + KMS notes from Paul, (5) run curl echo test with Acme sample.

alex-eng: I'll stand by to inspect raw event if curl returns 202 but Console still doesn't show trace links.

maria-sre: If they continue to hit 429s after uplift, we can route their Fluent Bit to a short-term buffer (S3) + async shipper to smooth spikes. Not ideal for realtime but workable for POC.

jordan-sales: Thanks all. I'll update thread with customer confirmation. :thumbsup:

acme-rep: Confirmed — starting test now. Will post results within 30m.

jordan-sales: received. ping when done.

acme-rep: Test done. curl returned 202 and echoed trace_id. Some 429s remain but much less.

sam-reliability: Great — uplift worked. Keep an eye on malformed JSON errors (maria noted) and batching.

jordan-sales: Closing loop: Tara will send pricing quote; Paul DM'd SOC2; Alex to check any remaining parsing glitches. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
